title: Blood vessels comparison sheet
subject: Science
unit: Spring 1: Muscles and bones (7C); the particle model (7G)
source: Seeded from science/y7 lesson 21 (Blood vessels comparison sheet (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 21: Blood vessels: arteries, veins and capillaries. To understand how the structure of each blood vessel suits its job

questions.q: Why do arteries have thick walls?
questions.a: Blood in them is at high pressure from the heart.
questions.model: Job: carry blood away from the heart. Condition: high pressure. Feature needed: strong, thick, elastic walls. So arteries have thick walls to withstand high pressure.

questions.q: Why are capillary walls so thin?
questions.a: So substances diffuse quickly between blood and cells.

questions.q: Which vessel carries blood back to the heart?
Core: Draw cross-sections of an artery, vein and capillary side by side and label one adaptation each.
questions.a: Artery: thick muscular wall, narrow space; vein: thin wall, wide space, valve; capillary: one-cell wall.
questions.model: Teacher draws the artery first: a thick ring with a small space in the middle, labelled 'thick muscle for high pressure'.

questions.q: Extend: Explain how veins in the legs get blood back up to the heart.
questions.a: Leg muscles squeeze the veins and valves stop blood falling back.

questions.q: Stretch: Explain why a cut artery is more dangerous than a cut vein.
questions.a: Blood is at high pressure, so it spurts out quickly and more is lost.

questions.q: Big question: why are arteries thick-walled but capillaries one cell thick?
questions.a: Arteries withstand high pressure; capillaries need thin walls for fast exchange.
